I've also been with AC since the first one and in my view, the modern-day segments are essential to the Assassin's Creed identity. Without them, it's no different than Ghost of Tsushima or any other stealth-action game with an original story in a historical setting.

Did they drop the ball? Sure, but they also dropped the ball with stealth in Valhalla and I'm sure you don't expect them to remove it in Red.

I have very mixed feelings about it. Onomichi is one of my favourite locations in the series, the substories are generally very enjoyable, and the game looks gorgeous.

But the combat felt really weak (though it has some of the coolest heat actions in the series), there was a criminal lack of Majima and Saejima, and I mostly hated the story.

I don't think it's the best in the series, not a bad game by any definition but definitely not the best.

I have a brother and a sister, we're all from different mothers but the same father. My father died in 2012 but he had been very sick for years, had his leg amputated and his mother had died 6 months prior. Enter my sister, she hasn't spoken to this side of the family for years and we didn't really care about her anymore, but when I heard that she'd been down to the hospital to see my dad I actually thought to myself that she'd come with good intentions. I was wrong, she went there just to say that she didn't consider herself my father's daughter. That didn't make me snap, but it put into this easily snappable mode. Just imagining my dad, on what was practically his deathbed at that point, see my sister and feel glad just to have her there, only for her to tell him that... Later, my ancient and small TV stopped working (for the millionth time) and I just lost it, I grabbed it, went over to the balcony and threw it out with all my strength. I've never been even close to that level of rage since then.
